fullPrompts.local: Create a completely independent research-guided hypothetical local terrain illustration for Galatea, Neptune's small inner moon. Landscape 16:9. This is an IMAGINED illustration, not an observed photograph or a registered Voyager location. Camera just above gently uneven ground: low irregular relief, modest shallow depressions, angular blocks scattered through fine grey granular regolith, varied small pebbles and subtle restrained grey tonal differences. Avoid recognizable features of Moon, Mars, Pluto, Ceres, Bennu, Miranda or any observed body's map; do not reference or reuse another body's geography. Galatea Voyager sources are tiny detections amid glare and do not resolve local terrain. Recent unresolved NIRSpec spectra show OH and a 2.72-micron feature interpreted through laboratory Mg-serpentine comparisons; they do not measure local material fractions, visible grey colour, rock grain sizes, landscape morphology, water ice absence, an ocean, a plume, or biology. Thus all depicted terrain, blocks, grain sizes, relief, chemistry/material fractions, grey colour, lighting and exposure are invented assumptions. Use a subdued low directional light from outside frame. Near-black sky is artistic transparency, not a measurement of atmospheric absence. No Neptune, Sun, stars, rings or other astronomical disk in this local view; no angular or raster-size claim. No haze, clouds, exposed liquid, rain, plume, ocean, vegetation, people, spacecraft, landing equipment or implication of survivable landing. No claim of tidal locking or a permanent Neptune-facing location. Composition: ground fills lower two thirds, low uneven horizon, dark upper third; natural restrained texture without dramatic mountains or enormous sharp craters. Place a clearly legible small pale footer on a dark strip: 'GALATEA — IMAGINED LOCAL VIEW' and a second line 'Terrain, materials, colour and lighting assumed; no observed site registration'. No other text or scale bar.
